newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac and Juppe see popularity rise.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac and Juppe see popularity rise.

text.p: The popularity of French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe showed a slight upturn this month, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.

The Louis Harris survey for the weekly Valeurs Actuelles said 32 percent of those asked were satisfied with the head of state, up from 29 percent in late November. Sixty percent had a poor opinion of him, against 64 percent in the previous survey.

The poll, based on a survey of 1,002 people conducted on January 2, highlighted a similar trend for Juppe, whose approval rating climbed to 26 percent from 20. The proportion of those dissatisfied with him fell to 67 percent from 73.

The trend checked a downward slide in the popularity of the two leaders. Popularity ratings for Chirac and Juppe have in recent months slumped to record lows in the face of austerity policies, rising unemployment and labour conflicts.
Sixty-two percent of those asked believed economic prospects were worsening, against 77 percent a month ago. Six percent thought things were improving, against three percent a month ago.
The poll was carried out two days after a televised New Year address in which Chirac promised more jobs and tax cuts in 1997.
